questions.text: How do you say 'Bonjour' in English in the morning ?
questions.explanation: We say 'Good morning' from sunrise to 12:00 (midday).

questions.text: If someone asks 'How are you?', what is a good answer ?
questions.explanation: 'How are you?' asks about your health. 'I am fine, thank you' is the standard polite response.

questions.text: True or False : We say 'Good night' when we meet someone at 8 PM.
questions.explanation: False! When we meet someone in the evening, we say 'Good evening'. 'Good night' is only used when leaving to go to bed or late at night to say goodbye.

questions.text: How do you ask someone's name ?
questions.explanation: To ask for someone's name, we use 'What is your name?'.

questions.text: Which word means 'Au revoir' ?
questions.explanation: 'Goodbye' or simply 'Bye' means au revoir.

Fiche_Lecon2_Unit1_In_The_Classroom.title: In the classroom (Dans la salle de classe)

questions.text: What is 'un stylo' in English ?
questions.explanation: A pen = un stylo. A pencil = un crayon de papier.

questions.text: What does the teacher say when he wants you to sit down ?
questions.explanation: 'Sit down' is the instruction for 'asseyez-vous'.

questions.text: True or False : 'A blackboard' means 'un tableau noir'.
questions.explanation: True. Black = noir, board = tableau.

questions.text: What is 'une gomme' in English ?
questions.explanation: An eraser (US) or a rubber (UK) is used to erase pencil marks.

questions.text: If a student wants to enter the classroom, what should they ask ?
questions.explanation: To ask for permission to enter, you politely say 'May I come in, please?'.

Fiche_Lecon3_Unit1_Locating_Classroom_Ob.title: Locating Classroom Objects (Où sont les objets ?)

questions.text: How do you ask where a pen is ?
questions.explanation: 'Where' is the question word used to ask about a place or location (Où est le stylo ?).

questions.text: If the book is SUR the desk, you say: The book is ... the desk.
questions.explanation: 'On' means sur (en contact). 'In' means dans, 'under' means sous.

questions.text: True or False : 'The bag is under the chair' means 'Le sac est sous la chaise'.
questions.explanation: True. 'Under' means 'sous'.

questions.text: Which preposition means 'dans' ?
questions.explanation: 'In' translates to 'dans' (inside something, like 'in the bag').

questions.text: Complete: The teacher is standing ... the blackboard.
questions.explanation: 'In front of' means 'devant'. The teacher usually stands in front of the board.

questions.text: What is 'un frère' in English ?
questions.explanation: A brother = un frère. A sister = une sœur.

questions.text: How do you say 'ma mère' in English ?
questions.explanation: My mother (or 'my mom') means 'ma mère'.

questions.text: True or False : 'Parents' in English only means your father and mother.
questions.explanation: True. Unlike French where 'parents' can mean all relatives, in English 'parents' strictly refers to father and mother.

questions.text: Who is your father's brother ?
questions.explanation: Your father's or mother's brother is your uncle (oncle).

questions.text: How do you ask someone how many brothers they have ?
options: How much brothers do you have?
How many brothers do you have?
questions.explanation: We use 'How many' to ask about quantities you can count (Combien de).

Fiche_Lecon5_Unit2_Sunday_With_My_Family.title: Sunday with my family (Dimanche en famille)

questions.text: What do people generally do on Sunday in English speaking countries ?
options: Rest and spend time with family
questions.explanation: Sunday (dimanche) is typically a day of rest (weekend) spent with family.

questions.text: How do you say 'nous regardons la télévision' ?
questions.explanation: The correct verb is 'to watch'. 'We watch TV' means nous regardons la télé.

questions.text: True or False : The present continuous (is/are + verb-ing) is used for an action happening right now.
questions.explanation: True. Example: 'I am playing' means 'Je suis en train de jouer' (en ce moment).

questions.text: What is the English word for 'le déjeuner' (le repas du midi) ?
questions.explanation: Breakfast = petit-déjeuner, Lunch = déjeuner, Dinner = dîner.

questions.text: Translate : 'My sister is playing in the garden.'
options: Ma sœur dort dans la chambre.
Ma sœur joue dans le jardin.
Mon frère joue dans le parc.
Ma sœur mange dans le jardin.
questions.explanation: Sister = sœur, is playing = joue / est en train de jouer, garden = jardin.

questions.text: What is 'la cuisine' (the room) in English ?
questions.explanation: The kitchen is the room where you prepare food and cook.

questions.text: How do you say 'une cuillère' in English ?
questions.explanation: A spoon = une cuillère. A fork = une fourchette. A knife = un couteau.

questions.text: True or False : 'A fridge' is short for refrigerator (réfrigérateur).
questions.explanation: True. It's the appliance used to keep food cold.

questions.text: Where do you wash the dishes ?
questions.explanation: The sink (l'évier) is where you use water to wash the dishes (la vaisselle).

questions.text: What is the English word for 'une assiette' ?
questions.explanation: A plate is a flat dish used for eating food.

Fiche_Lecon7_Unit3_Whats_the_Date.title: What's the date ? (Quelle est la date ?)

questions.text: How do you say 'Janvier' in English ?
questions.explanation: The first month of the year is January.

questions.text: What is the correct format for dates in British English ?
questions.explanation: In the UK (and often taught in CI), the format is Day-Month-Year (ex: 12th May). In the US, it's Month-Day (May 12th).

questions.text: True or False : Days of the week (Monday, Tuesday...) and Months always start with a capital letter in English.
questions.explanation: True. Unlike French (lundi, janvier), in English they must be capitalized: Monday, January.

questions.text: How do you write 'le premier' (the 1st) for a date ?
questions.explanation: For dates, we use ordinal numbers. 1 = first (1st), 2 = second (2nd), 3 = third (3rd).

questions.text: If today is 'Wednesday', what is tomorrow ?
questions.explanation: Wednesday = Mercredi. Thursday = Jeudi.

questions.text: How do you ask 'Quelle heure est-il ?' in English ?
questions.explanation: The standard question is 'What time is it?'.

questions.text: What does 'It's three o'clock' mean ?
questions.explanation: We use 'o'clock' only for full, exact hours (l'heure juste, pile).

questions.text: True or False : 'Half past four' means 'Il est 4h30'.
questions.explanation: True. 'Half' means demi (30 minutes), and 'past' means 'passé de'. Donc 30 min passées après 4h = 4h30.

questions.text: How do you say 'Il est 8h15' ?
questions.explanation: 15 minutes = a quarter. 'Past' = après. So 'a quarter past eight' = un quart d'heure passé après 8h.

questions.text: What does 'A.M.' stand for when talking about time (ex: 8:00 a.m.) ?
questions.explanation: A.M. is used for morning hours (from midnight to 11:59). P.M. is for afternoon/evening (from noon to 23:59).

questions.text: What preposition is used before time? (ex: We have English ... 8 o'clock)
questions.explanation: In English, we always use 'at' for time. 'At 8 o'clock' = à 8 heures.

questions.text: What does a timetable show ?
options: The schedule of subjects and classes for the week (l'emploi du temps)
questions.explanation: A timetable (or schedule) is the plan of your lessons (emploi du temps).

questions.text: Vrai ou Faux : On utilise la préposition 'on' avant les jours de la semaine (ex: 'On Monday').
questions.explanation: Vrai. We say 'at 8 o'clock' (pour l'heure) but 'on Monday' (pour les jours).

questions.text: How do you ask about someone's favourite subject ?
questions.explanation: 'Subject' means 'matière scolaire'. 'Favourite' = préféré.

questions.text: If a student says 'I'm late!', what does it mean ?
questions.explanation: To be late means to arrive after the expected time (être en retard).

Fiche_Lecon10_Unit4_My_Father_Is_A_Polic.title: My father is a policeman (Les métiers)

questions.text: What is a 'policeman' ?
questions.explanation: Policeman = policier (ou agent de police).

questions.text: How do you ask 'Quel est ton métier ?' in English ?
options: What is your job? (or What do you do?)
questions.explanation: 'Job' means métier/profession. 'What do you do?' is also very common.

questions.text: True or False : A 'nurse' works in a school.
questions.explanation: False! A nurse (infirmière / infirmier) works in a hospital or clinic.

questions.text: Who works in a school to teach students ?
questions.explanation: A teacher = un professeur / un enseignant.

questions.text: What does a 'farmer' do ?
options: He works on a farm growing crops or raising animals (agriculteur)
questions.explanation: A farmer is an agriculteur/fermier. 'Farm' = la ferme.

questions.text: What does a mechanic use to fix cars ?
questions.explanation: A mechanic uses tools like a spanner to repair cars.

questions.text: Who uses a chalk and a blackboard ?
questions.explanation: A teacher (professeur) uses a chalk (craie) to write on a blackboard (tableau noir).

questions.text: Vrai ou Faux : A 'tailor' (tailleur) uses a needle and thread.
questions.explanation: Vrai. A tailor makes clothes and uses a needle (aiguille) and thread (fil).

questions.text: What is the English word for 'le lieu de travail' ?
questions.explanation: A workplace is the place where someone does their job.

questions.text: What does a doctor use to listen to your heart ?
questions.explanation: A doctor (médecin) uses a stethoscope.

questions.text: What do you wear on your feet before putting on shoes ?
questions.explanation: Socks are worn on the feet.

questions.text: How do you say 'une robe' in English ?
questions.explanation: A dress = une robe. A skirt = une jupe.

questions.text: True or False : 'Trousers' (pantalon) is always plural in English.
questions.explanation: True. We say 'my trousers are black' (comme pantalon a deux jambes).

questions.text: What is a 'shirt' ?
questions.explanation: A shirt is une chemise. (A t-shirt = un t-shirt).

questions.text: What do you wear on your head to protect from the sun ?
questions.explanation: A hat = un chapeau.

questions.text: What colour is the sky on a sunny day ?
questions.explanation: Blue = bleu.

questions.text: How do you translate 'une chemise rouge' ?
questions.explanation: In English, the adjective (colour) always comes BEFORE the noun: A red shirt.

questions.text: True or False : Adjectives in English do not take an 's' in the plural.
questions.explanation: True. Adjectives are invariable. We say 'Red shirts' (des chemises rouges), the 's' is only on the noun.

questions.text: What is the colour of grass (l'herbe) ?
questions.explanation: Green = vert.

questions.text: Translate : 'Il porte un pantalon noir.'
options: He is wearing a black shirt.
questions.explanation: He is wearing (il porte) + black (noir) + trousers (pantalon).

questions.text: How do you say 'J'aime le riz' ?
questions.explanation: 'I like' = J'aime. 'Rice' = le riz.

questions.text: What is the opposite of 'I like' ?
questions.explanation: To express dislike, you say 'I do not like' or 'I don't like'.

questions.text: Vrai ou Faux : 'Meat' signifie la viande.
questions.explanation: Vrai. Meat = viande. Fish = poisson.

questions.text: Which of these is a drink (une boisson) ?
questions.explanation: Water, Coke (Coca), milk (lait) are drinks. The others are solid food.

questions.text: If you are very hungry, what do you say ?
questions.explanation: 'Hungry' = avoir faim. 'Thirsty' = avoir soif.

questions.text: What is a 'banana' ?
questions.explanation: Banana = banane.

questions.text: Which of these is a vegetable (un légume) ?
questions.explanation: A carrot is a vegetable. Oranges, apples and mangoes are fruits.

questions.text: True or False : 'An apple a day keeps the doctor away' is a famous English proverb.
questions.explanation: True. It means eating healthy fruits (like an apple) keeps you in good health.

questions.text: How do you say 'Je veux des tomates' ?
questions.explanation: 'I want' = je veux.

questions.text: What colour is a ripe lemon (un citron mûr) ?
questions.explanation: A lemon is yellow.

questions.text: What does the verb 'to boil' mean ?
questions.explanation: 'To boil' means to cook in very hot water (bouillir).

questions.text: If you want to make chips (frites), you must ... the potatoes in oil.
questions.explanation: 'To fry' means to cook in hot fat or oil (frire).

questions.text: True or False : 'To cut' means 'couper'.
questions.explanation: True. You cut the vegetables with a knife.

questions.text: Before eating fruits or vegetables, what should you do first ?
questions.explanation: 'To wash' means laver. It is important for hygiene.

questions.text: What does 'to mix' mean ?
questions.explanation: To mix means to combine ingredients together (mélanger).

questions.text: How do you say 'Je me brosse les dents' in English ?
questions.explanation: To brush = brosser. Teeth = les dents.

questions.text: What do you use to clean your body in the shower ?
questions.explanation: Soap is used for washing to kill germs and remove dirt.

questions.text: True or False : 'To have a bath' means 'Prendre un bain'.
questions.explanation: True. 'To have a shower' means prendre une douche.

questions.text: What should you do before eating and after using the toilet ?
options: Wash your hands (se laver les mains)
questions.explanation: Washing your hands is the most basic rule of body hygiene.

questions.text: What is a 'towel' ?
questions.explanation: A towel is used to dry your body after a shower.

questions.text: What does 'insalubrity' mean ?
questions.explanation: Insalubrity refers to places that are dirty, full of rubbish and dangerous for health.

questions.text: Mosquitoes (les moustiques) can transmit which disease ?
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes breed in dirty, stagnant water and transmit malaria.

questions.text: True or False : Keeping your environment clean helps prevent diseases.
questions.explanation: True. A clean environment stops germs and insects from multiplying.

questions.text: What is the English word for 'ordures' or 'poubelle' ?
questions.explanation: Rubbish (UK) or Garbage (US) means ordures. The bin is la poubelle.

questions.text: If you are sick with malaria, who should you see ?
questions.explanation: You should go to the hospital to see a doctor.

questions.text: Where do you go to buy clothes ?
questions.explanation: You buy clothes in a shop (un magasin) or at the market (au marché).

questions.text: How do you ask for the price of a shirt ?
questions.explanation: 'How much' is used to ask for the price (combien ça coûte).

questions.text: True or False : 'Expensive' means 'cher'.
questions.explanation: True. If a shirt costs a lot of money, it is expensive. The opposite is 'cheap'.

questions.text: If the seller says 'It's 5,000 CFA', what is he talking about ?
questions.explanation: He is giving the price of the item.

questions.text: What does 'Can I try it on?' mean ?
questions.explanation: To try on means 'essayer' (un vêtement) to see if the size is right.
